doctrine: HIGGSFIELD AS VIRTUAL PRODUCTION STUDIO: The platform is architected in three layers (Features/Models/Apps), not a single prompt-in-video-out tool. Seven Laws govern operation: (1) Features First, Models Second (choose output type before engine); (2) Identity Before Everything (lock Soul ID with 20-30 reference photos); (3) Compound the Library (Shots app: 1 image into 9 angles, 9x multiplier); (4) Prompt Like a Director (Composition+Subject+Camera Move+Mood); (5) Shot Structure at Top (declare duration/shots/aspect ratio first); (6) Name What the Camera is NOT Doing (negative constraints lock variables); (7) Sequential Never Parallel (pre-production -> production -> post). PRODUCTION PIPELINE: Pre-production builds assets (Soul ID, master keyframes, prop sheets, shot library via Shots/Outfit Swap/Angles/Skin Enhancer). Production animates with appropriate model routed by content type. Post-production reviews, upscales, exports. CONSISTENCY SYSTEM: Character reference tagged explicitly in every prompt with role notation (<<<image_1>>> is character reference). Style references separate. Previous scene's video fed as context for continuity. Start Frame and End Frame lock visual anchors. Preservation constraints explicit when editing. FEATURE TAXONOMY: Cinema Studio (cinematic camera language, dolly moves, depth of field), Lipsync Studio (dialogue, lip-sync to audio), Vibe Motion (structured motion design for infographics/decks), AI Influencer Studio (parametric character building), Draw/Sketch to Video, Click to Ad, UGC Factory, Marketing Studio, Soul Cinema (keyframe generation), Soul Cast (character reference sheets), Soul Photodump (lifestyle aesthetic), Popcorn (storyboards). MODEL TAXONOMY: Kling 3.0 (multi-shot sequences, multi-character), Kling 2.6 (performance, dialogue, native audio), WAN 2.6 (cinematic continuity, narrative), Seedance 2.0 (action, animation, transformation, POV), Sora 2/2 Pro (photorealism, physics), Minimax Hailuo 02 (fast iteration), Google Veo 3.1, Nano Banana Pro (keyframes), Flux 2 (detailed images), Soul 2.0 (photorealistic portraiture). FORCE-MULTIPLIER APPS: Shots (9 angles from 1 master image, 9x multiplier), Outfit Swap (wardrobe variation per scene), Angles (change camera perspective), Skin Enhancer (consistent texture), Upscale (image and video), Face Swap Extension, Reference Extension, Banana/Product Placement. PROMPT ARCHITECTURE: Universal structure: shot structure declaration (top) -> reference tags (character/style/environment roles) -> style block (Film Quality Block template) -> timed segments (named time blocks 0-3s, 3-6s) -> camera behavior (including negatives) -> negative constraints. Shot-level formula: Composition+Subject+Camera Move+Mood. FIVE SEEDANCE RECIPES (15-second formats): (1) Transformations (6 shots, escalation arc calm-threat-transformation-combat-return), (2) Orbs (1 shot first-person POV, handheld chaos, bracket VFX), (3) POVs (locked first-person, negative constraint: no cuts/zoom/stabilization), (4) Fights (choreography beat-by-beat, speed ramps, power mismatch), (5) Animation (timed blocks, stylistic aesthetic specified, physics descriptions). MONETIZATION ARCHITECTURE: (1) Higgsfield Earn (daily posting, 3x posts per day outperforms weekly, performance-based payments); (2) AI Influencer Agency (monthly retainer, Soul ID + content calendar); (3) AI-Native Brand Kits (one-time package: Soul ID + 10-20 image library + style guide + prompt templates); (4) 24-Hour Brand Launch (premium velocity-based pricing); (5) Cinematic B-Roll Packs (themed 30-60 clip libraries); (6) Prompt Packs and Preset Libraries (niche-specific collections); (7) Recurring Video Series (subscription model for weekly content with locked avatar). POSITIONING: Position as Virtual Production Studio (studio-in-a-box for solopreneurs), NOT AI prompting. Sell consistency and systemization, not randomized output. Premium recurring pricing for agencies and SMB buyers. COMMERCIAL BLUEPRINT ($350k reference): (1) Build characters in Soul Cast (genre, budget, era, archetype, identity, physique, eyes, hair, outfit); (2) Build locations with atmospheric specificity (not just visual description, include emotional context); (3) Generate scene keyframe combining characters and location; (4) Write shot-level dialogue prompts with explicit character references and per-shot choreography; (5) Animate with model routed for content (Kling for dialogue, WAN for continuity); (6) Apply Cinema Studio presets (lens, camera move); (7) Upscale and assemble. FOUR MINDSET SHIFTS: (1) Prompt to pipeline (better pipeline, not better prompt); (2) Model loyalty to model routing (keep whole roster, route each shot to best engine); (3) Generating to directing (director's notes not screenplay); (4) Scarcity to compounding (library compounds, not individual generations). MULTI-SCENE PRODUCTION: Cross-style consistency method: (1) Create character keyframe and prop sheet (multi-angle orthographic) before any scenes; (2) Generate per-scene keyframes in Soul Cinema; (3) Edit keyframes with Nano Banana Pro preserving everything else explicitly; (4) Animate with Seedance using keyframe+character reference+previous scene as context; (5) Use transition devices (portal, watch activation, white flash) for clean visual breaks between styles. Seven production-tested styles: 2D Anime, French Graphic Novel/Moebius, Chibi Low-Poly, 3D Claymation, Black & White Manga, 2D Cartoon in Live Action, Live-Action Cinematic.

prompts: Transformation formula: 6 shots, 15 seconds, escalation arc (calm-threat-transformation-combat-return-calm), numbered shots, each describing exact action, no 3D/cartoon/VFX for realism, optional visual gag in background

Orb formula: 1 shot, 15 seconds, first-person POV as character's eyes, hyper-chaotic handheld, wide-angle with distortion, bracket-syntax VFX inline, three-beat action (engagement-escalation-titanic finish), RAMPS TO SLOW MOTION on key beat, SFX block at end
POV formula: 1 shot, 15 seconds, first-person locked perspective, explicit negative constraint (no cuts, no zoom, natural head movement), short prompts often win

Fight formula: clear location with atmospheric specificity, power mismatch (size/weapon/style), escalation arc (setup-first strike-counter-climax-resolution), speed ramps inline, beat-by-beat choreography, physics as precisely as actions

Animation formula: keyframe as style reference, specify aesthetic in opening line, break 15 seconds into timed blocks (0-3s, 3-6s, 6-9s, 9-12s, 12-15s), describe physics as precisely as actions, close with technical spec (fps, aspect, effects)
Film Quality Block standard: cinematic lighting, photorealistic, 35mm film quality, professional color grading, sharp focus, film grain, depth of field mastery, ARRI ALEXA aesthetic

Film Quality Block ultra-realism: grounded realism, strong 35mm film look, heavy film grain, sharp but imperfect focus, noticeable focus breathing, motion blur on fast actions, halation on highlights, soft highlight rolloff, slightly desaturated tones, practical VFX feel, minimal CGI look, natural imperfections, add 'no 3D, no cartoon, no VFX' to kill plastic skin

Luxury advertising block: shallow depth of field (background blurred, foreground sharp), soft diffused lighting (no harsh shadows, gentle even illumination), highlights not blown out (shadows lifted, airy), warm interior light (sense of occasion), color graded warm with slight deep green in dark areas, luxury advertising aesthetic (polished, warm tones, aspirational mood)
Shot-level dialogue formula: shot number, composition+camera behavior, performance note, explicit reference tag (<<<image_1>>> is character), dialogue in quotes
Location prompt formula: location name + visual specificity + atmosphere clause (emotional tone + narrative context)
Character reference in prompt: '<<<image_1>>> is the character reference AND visual style reference...'
Negative camera constraint: 'No cuts, no zoom, natural head movement' for POV preservation
Multi-reference syntax: <<<image_1>>> is character, <<<image_2>>> is style, <<<image_3>>> is environment, instruct model to ignore everything else

operating_rules: Features First, Models Second: decide what you're making before deciding what powers it
Identity Before Everything: train Soul ID or build AI Influencer character before generating any video
Compound the Library: one image becomes nine shots via Shots app; leverage is in asset library compounding, not individual generations
Prompt Like a Director: Composition+Subject+Camera Move+Mood; one clean camera move beats three stacked
Shot Structure Goes at Top: declare number of shots, duration, aspect ratio before describing content
Name What the Camera is NOT Doing: explicit negative constraints lock variables (no cuts, no zoom, natural head movement)
Sequential Never Parallel: pre-production -> production -> post, each step builds on the last, skip upstream steps and downstream compounds to wasted credits
Post Daily to Higgsfield Earn without exception: 3 posts per day outperforms 1 post per week due to performance data density
Lean Toward Volume Over Per-Post Perfection: algorithm rewards data density, consistency compounds
AI Influencer Doesn't Get Tired: use the 24/7 advantage, your character doesn't need breaks
Character Consistency is the Entire Game: unlock locked identity and pay inconsistency tax on every regeneration
Invest in Master Keyframe Before Animation: everything downstream inherits lighting, framing, DOF, color grade
Review Like an Editor, Change One Variable at a Time: changing multiple variables destroys diagnostics, adjust (image OR camera move OR prompt OR model) and regenerate
Upscale at End of Each Stage, Not Mid-Pipeline: Image Upscale before animation, Video Upscale at finish
Store Every Asset in Organized Project Folders: library compounds across projects
Reference Role Assignment: assign character/style/environment roles and instruct model to ignore everything else
Preservation Constraints Explicit: when editing, state what must NOT change (lighting, environment, camera angle)
Run Master Image Through Shots, Outfit Swap, Skin Enhancer Before Any Animation: pre-production assets multiplied via apps
Separate Character and Style References: tag them with explicit role notation (<<<image_1>>> character, <<<image_2>>> style only)
Feed Previous Scene's Video as Context for Next Generation: multi-scene continuity maintained
Start Frame Locks Opening Look, End Frame Locks Clean Finish: directional control in Cinema Studio
One Deliberate Camera Move Per Shot: beats three stacked moves
Declare Shot Structure Before Content: number of shots, duration, aspect ratio at prompt top
Negative Constraints for Precision: state explicitly what is NOT happening in the scene
Production Pipeline is Sequential: pre-production (identity/keyframes/props/shot library) -> production (animation/camera/model) -> post (review/upscale/assembly)

weird_gold: The counter-intuitive insight: freaky/unusual AI characters (forest-dwelling with mushroom features, iridescent skin) outperform photorealistic models posting identical content because they stop scrolling
Luxury advertising does not require expensive post-production grading; the look is in the Cinema Studio preset (35mm f/1.4), not the grade
Sometimes the shortest prompts hit hardest; the Horses POV example is a single sentence
The model decision tree is fast: 30 seconds from blank screen to routed generation by asking five binary questions
Sora 2 Enhancer with Deflickering is not a standard upscaler; it is trained specifically to eliminate frame instability characteristic of AI video by analyzing motion across frames
The Archetypes slot (Lover, Hero, Trickster, Mentor, Shadow) in Soul Cast encodes relational function in narrative, giving the model behavioral-pattern priors that physical description cannot supply
Transition devices (watch activation, portal, white flash) convert style shifts into plot beats the viewer expects to look different, making jarring visual discontinuity narratively coherent
Kling 2.6 native audio matching is done by listing sounds in sequence at the end of the prompt; the model matches them to on-screen actions with no secondary audio pass required
Running every master image through Shots before any animation separates the 9x multiplier insight from the generation insight; the operator builds a shot library in pre-production, not post
The compounding insight: every asset trained, every shot library built, every prop sheet generated, every preset saved is a reusable asset; leverage lives in the library, not any single generation
